scope: S11-S20 original scenes; manually scored before drafting. No automated semantic scoring.

cards.title: Only You
cards.instruction: Choose one person as the only one you trust. Seek their help while hiding how much you depend on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can you check my resignation letter? Just the spelling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The spelling's fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And resigning? Does that word suit me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ask your manager.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you ask? I'd trust the answer more in your voice.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 disguises a life decision as a spelling check; A3 tests suitability; A5 will trust the manager only through B.

responseLogic.evidence: Spelling approval lets A broaden the question; the manager suggestion makes A recruit B as intermediary.

relationship.evidence: B answers the limited request then proposes a more relevant person; A refuses to transfer trust.

heightening.evidence: A5 extends reliance from checking a letter to mediating another person answer.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a resignation letter and its purportedly small request without narration.

brevityWit.evidence: Does that word suit me reveals the concealed decision; in your voice follows the referral directly.

records.recommendedEdit: Retain: the refusal to transfer trust develops the spelling pretext. The final admission exposes more dependence than A intended.
records.principalWeakness: No acceptance-blocking weakness; specific reservations are retained in the evidence.
records.firstPassCausality: Spelling approval lets A broaden the question; the manager suggestion makes A recruit B as intermediary.

cards.title: Only You
cards.instruction: Choose one person as the only one you trust. Seek their help while hiding how much you depend on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're coming to the dentist with me, aren't you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The dentist knows what to do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. I need you to confirm that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not a dentist.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. You have no professional reason to defend the drill.

cardFidelity.evidence: Only B can supply reassurance, but A1 and A3 openly ask for attendance and confirmation rather than concealing dependence.

responseLogic.evidence: Dentist competence prompts a request to confirm it; B non-expertise becomes a reason to trust B over the drill.

relationship.evidence: B states two sensible facts but cannot change the proposed arrangement.

heightening.evidence: A5 invents a professional bias against the drill rather than revealing a new cover for needing B.

specificity.evidence: Dentist visit and accompanying friend are clear, economical facts.

brevityWit.evidence: The drill defense is a compact twist, though it shifts the game toward mistrust of professionals.

records.recommendedEdit: Rewrite: give A a practical pretext for needing this particular companion and let B solve that pretext, forcing A to find a closer form of help.
records.principalWeakness: Rewrite: give A a practical pretext for needing this particular companion and let B solve that pretext, forcing A to find a closer form of help.
records.firstPassCausality: Dentist competence prompts a request to confirm it; B non-expertise becomes a reason to trust B over the drill.

cards.title: After What Happened
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as if an unnamed past incident still hangs over the interaction. Read ordinary remarks through that memory.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put out the blue cups. So we're doing this again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're the only clean ones.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's how it started last time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll wash the red cups.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please don't call that a fresh start.

cardFidelity.evidence: Blue cups and clean ones trigger ominous recognition while the incident stays unnamed.

responseLogic.evidence: Only-clean explanation becomes repetition of the past; washing red cups prompts a fresh-start phrase B never used.

relationship.evidence: B offers to change cups, but the precise remedy hardly matters to the last line.

heightening.evidence: A5 rejects an invented label instead of using the new choice B offers.

specificity.evidence: The cups and washing keep the situation immediately understandable.

brevityWit.evidence: Fresh start relies on a washing pun and could follow many unrelated offers.

records.recommendedEdit: Rewrite B remedy and A final interpretation so an exact ordinary phrase becomes the troubling echo; leave the incident unnamed.
records.principalWeakness: Rewrite B remedy and A final interpretation so an exact ordinary phrase becomes the troubling echo; leave the incident unnamed.
records.firstPassCausality: Only-clean explanation becomes repetition of the past; washing red cups prompts a fresh-start phrase B never used.

cards.title: Envious Admiration
cards.instruction: Be sincerely impressed by another player while trying not to appear lesser. Compliment, imitate, and compete at the same time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your pie crust is gorgeous. I've copied the lattice with smaller gaps.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You didn't need to improve it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Improve? I'm celebrating you more precisely.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Would you like my recipe?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please. I'll return it with respectful corrections.

cardFidelity.evidence: A admires and copies the lattice but celebrating more precisely and promised corrections make the admiration sound glib.

responseLogic.evidence: B objects to improvement and A denies it; recipe offer produces a generic plan to correct any recipe.

relationship.evidence: B shares generously at B4, though the specific recipe contributes no new practical constraint.

heightening.evidence: A5 repeats competitive improvement rather than discovering a new way to keep up.

specificity.evidence: Pie crust, lattice and recipe establish a clear shared craft.

brevityWit.evidence: Respectful corrections restates the contradiction more than enacting it.

records.recommendedEdit: Rewrite around a useful recipe detail B offers; show A eagerly adopting it while trying to find one smaller area of superiority.
records.principalWeakness: Rewrite around a useful recipe detail B offers; show A eagerly adopting it while trying to find one smaller area of superiority.
records.firstPassCausality: B objects to improvement and A denies it; recipe offer produces a generic plan to correct any recipe.

brevityWit.evidence: Using that too requires B exact confident disclaimer; the imitation remains sincere.

records.principalWeakness: No acceptance-blocking weakness; specific reservations are retained in the evidence.

cards.title: The Old You
cards.instruction: Perform the person you used to be, even when that identity no longer fits. Defend the old version of yourself whenever it is challenged.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put 'Lightning' on my retirement cake. That's what the band called me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake says Graham.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Graham worked in accounts. Lightning had a smoke machine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a small family party.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then get a small smoke machine.

cardFidelity.evidence: A defends a former band identity against the retirement name and present family scale.

responseLogic.evidence: Graham on the cake causes a split between accountant and performer; small party makes A reduce the smoke machine size rather than give it up.

relationship.evidence: B wants a suitable family celebration and supplies both its existing cake and limited scale.

heightening.evidence: A accommodates size while insisting on the old identity signature prop.

specificity.evidence: Retirement cake, band nickname and family party establish past and present through speech.

brevityWit.evidence: Small smoke machine uses B adjective to preserve the old performance.

records.recommendedEdit: Retain: B limits the event and A fits the old self into that exact limit.
records.principalWeakness: No acceptance-blocking weakness; specific reservations are retained in the evidence.
records.firstPassCausality: Graham on the cake causes a split between accountant and performer; small party makes A reduce the smoke machine size rather than give it up.

cards.title: Replacement Fear
cards.instruction: Behave as if your place is insecure. Make yourself indispensable and treat small changes as threats.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why does the new receptionist have a key? I open this office.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could take a day off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And let the door forget me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a spare key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll keep it safe. Spares are my department too.

cardFidelity.evidence: A treats a newcomer key as a threat and takes ownership of the backup task to remain indispensable.

responseLogic.evidence: A day-off offer evokes being forgotten; the spare-key reassurance becomes another job A claims.

relationship.evidence: B intends to provide cover so A can take leave and clarifies the backup role.

heightening.evidence: A expands duties to absorb the very provision meant to make A replaceable for a day.

specificity.evidence: Receptionist, office entry and spare key form a clear workplace change.

brevityWit.evidence: The door forgetting A is a figurative admission of insecurity; spares my department follows B label.

records.recommendedEdit: Retain: spare is a specific new category A takes over. The personified door can be played as anxious exaggeration.
records.principalWeakness: No acceptance-blocking weakness; specific reservations are retained in the evidence.
records.firstPassCausality: A day-off offer evokes being forgotten; the spare-key reassurance becomes another job A claims.

cards.title: For Their Own Good
cards.instruction: Take charge of another person's choices because you trust your judgment more than theirs. Frame control as care.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've ordered you the mild curry. You're welcome.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wanted the hot one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's exactly the impulse I'm protecting you from.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order it myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've told the waiter not to believe you.

cardFidelity.evidence: A orders for B, calls contrary preference an impulse requiring protection, and has pre-empted B ability to override it.

responseLogic.evidence: Hot preference is recast as the problem care prevents; self-ordering meets A advance instruction to the waiter.

relationship.evidence: B wants the hot curry and proposes ordering directly, a credible independent route.

heightening.evidence: A has extended protective control beyond the meal choice to whose account the waiter should trust.

specificity.evidence: Curry order and restaurant waiter establish the whole dispute.

brevityWit.evidence: Not to believe you reveals a concrete layer of anticipatory control caused by B proposed bypass.

records.recommendedEdit: Retain: the pre-empted workaround is understandable as A already taken precaution; it needs no narrator.
records.principalWeakness: No acceptance-blocking weakness; specific reservations are retained in the evidence.
records.firstPassCausality: Hot preference is recast as the problem care prevents; self-ordering meets A advance instruction to the waiter.

cards.title: For Their Own Good

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: Their Opinion Matters
cards.instruction: Seek one person's approval while pretending their opinion is irrelevant. Adjust yourself whenever they respond.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What do you think of my blue shirt? Purely academic.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I prefer the green one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So do I. This is my changing shirt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Wear whatever makes you happy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you sound happier about the blue?

cardFidelity.evidence: Academic pretense and agreement about green show concealed approval-seeking; A5 asks B to change their response rather than adjusting A choice.

responseLogic.evidence: Green preference prompts a changing-shirt excuse; makes-you-happy advice prompts happier tone about blue, leaving A direction unclear.

relationship.evidence: B answers honestly and offers autonomy, giving A room to choose.

heightening.evidence: A5 exposes dependence but retreats to the original shirt with no clear change in strategy.

specificity.evidence: Two shirt colors establish a simple immediate choice.

brevityWit.evidence: Changing shirt is a revealing cover; the final happier request is less specific in what A will do.

records.recommendedEdit: Rewrite so B second response causes a further visible adjustment by A while A maintains a casual pretext.
records.principalWeakness: Rewrite so B second response causes a further visible adjustment by A while A maintains a casual pretext.
records.firstPassCausality: Green preference prompts a changing-shirt excuse; makes-you-happy advice prompts happier tone about blue, leaving A direction unclear.

cards.title: Their Opinion Matters
cards.instruction: Seek one person's approval while pretending their opinion is irrelevant. Adjust yourself whenever they respond.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Would you like a compliment?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, no. Just look at it from the difficult angle.

responseLogic.evidence: Books held prompts a count; offered compliment prompts an unspecified difficult angle that would fit many crafted objects.

heightening.evidence: A5 adds a vague viewing instruction rather than a concrete fresh display of skill.

specificity.evidence: Shelf and forty-seven books establish an understandable boast.

brevityWit.evidence: From wood and difficult angle supply mild absurdity without showing what deserves attention.

records.recommendedEdit: Let B cooperate with an actual task, then offer a practical use of the shelf that A redirects toward a specific display of workmanship.
records.principalWeakness: Let B cooperate with an actual task, then offer a practical use of the shelf that A redirects toward a specific display of workmanship.

cards.instruction: Treat every development as urgent evidence of a crisis. Escalate precautions faster than the facts justify.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I spilled it.

beats.text: Good. We've identified the source. Stop producing water.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've wiped it up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Where's the cloth? The threat has changed location.

cardFidelity.evidence: A interprets a spill as evacuation, its source as a threat and cleanup as displacement of danger.

responseLogic.evidence: B owning the spill prompts source containment; wiping it up relocates the imagined crisis into the cloth.

heightening.evidence: The successful cleanup makes A expand the search rather than reduce precautions.

specificity.evidence: Kettle, droplet, wiping and cloth keep the physical facts consistent.

brevityWit.evidence: Changed location follows the actual cleanup, and cannot be used unchanged after a different remedy.

records.firstPassCausality: B owning the spill prompts source containment; wiping it up relocates the imagined crisis into the cloth.
